source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: ABG: pH 7.28, PaCO2 38, HCO3 16. This is:
questions.rationale: Low pH with low bicarbonate and normal CO2 is metabolic acidosis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Metabolic Acidosis (PDF p. 402)
questions.quote: Expected blood gas changes include a low pH (less than 7.35) and a low bicarbonate level

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Severe diarrhea leads to which acid-base imbalance?
questions.rationale: Diarrhea causes excess bicarbonate elimination.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Metabolic Acidosis (PDF p. 402)
questions.quote: Excesseliminationofbicarbonateions (diarrhea).

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Deep, rapid breathing in metabolic acidosis is the body's attempt to:
questions.rationale: Hyperventilation compensates by lowering CO2.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Metabolic Acidosis (PDF p. 402)
questions.quote: Rapid, deep breathing (hyperventilation) as body attempts to compensate

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with prolonged vomiting has a high pH and high bicarbonate. The nurse identifies:
questions.rationale: High pH and high HCO3 from gastric acid loss.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Metabolic Alkalosis (PDF p. 402)
questions.quote: Prolonged vomiting or nasogastric suctioning

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which replacement is given for metabolic alkalosis with hypokalemia?
questions.rationale: KCl replaces both potassium and chloride losses.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Metabolic Alkalosis (PDF p. 402)
questions.quote: potassium is administered as KCI to replace both K and CI losses

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with sedative overdose has RR 6/min. Expected ABG imbalance:
questions.rationale: Hypoventilation retains CO2, causing respiratory acidosis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Respiratory Acidosis (PDF p. 403)
questions.quote: Overdose of sedatives

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: An anxious client hyperventilates and reports lightheadedness. The nurse expects:
questions.rationale: Hyperventilation blows off CO2; coach slow breathing.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Respiratory Alkalosis (PDF p. 403)
questions.quote: Respiratory alkalosis is always caused by hyperventilation

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which nursing action helps an anxious client with respiratory alkalosis?
questions.rationale: Slow breathing or rebreathing allows CO2 to accumulate.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Respiratory Alkalosis (PDF p. 403)
questions.quote: the patient is instructed to breathe more slowly to allow CO2 to accumulate

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A burn with blisters, mottled red base, weeping, and severe pain is:
questions.rationale: Second-degree burns are blistered, weeping, and painful; full thickness is painless and leathery.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Burn Depth (PDF p. 404)
questions.quote: Weeping surface, edema

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A burn that is dry, leathery, white, and painless is:
questions.rationale: Third-degree burns destroy nerve endings; grafting is needed.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Burn Depth (PDF p. 404)
questions.quote: Dry, pale white, leathery or charred

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Using the rule of nines, an adult with burns on the entire front of the chest and abdomen and one entire arm has:
questions.rationale: Anterior trunk 18% + one arm 9% = 27%.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Rule of 9's (PDF p. 405)
questions.quote: Arms- 9 % each

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: For scattered small burns, the size of the client's palm represents about:
questions.rationale: Palm method: palm ≈ 1% TBSA.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Palm Method (PDF p. 405)
questions.quote: the size of the patient’s palm is approximately 1 % of TBSA

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which burn is classified as major regardless of size?
options: Burn of the face or hands
questions.rationale: Burns to face, eyes, ears, hands, feet, perineum, joints, and inhalation or electrical injury are major.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Extent of Burn (PDF p. 405)
questions.quote: All burns involving eyes, ears, face, hands, feet, perineum, joints.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A burn method that adjusts body-part percentages by age is the:
questions.rationale: Lund and Browder is more accurate and age-adjusted.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Estimating TBSA (PDF p. 405)
questions.quote: Modifies percentages for body segments according to age.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: An electrical burn victim needs cardiac monitoring mainly because of:
questions.rationale: Current through the body causes ventricular fibrillation and internal damage.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Electrical Burns (PDF p. 405)
questions.quote: associated with cardiopulmonary arrest, ventricular fibrillation

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Singed nasal hair, sooty sputum, and hoarseness after a fire suggest:
questions.rationale: These signs indicate smoke inhalation; monitor airway closely.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Smoke Inhalation (PDF p. 406)
questions.quote: Singed nasal hair

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Cherry-red skin and headache after a fire in an enclosed room suggest:
questions.rationale: CO binds hemoglobin about 200 times more than oxygen.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Carbon Monoxide (PDF p. 406)
questions.quote: Bright cherry red, in face and upper torso.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Oxygen for CO poisoning is continued until carboxyhemoglobin is below:
questions.rationale: Give oxygen until COHb is less than 5%.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Carbon Monoxide (PDF p. 406)
questions.quote: Oxygen is administered until the carboxyhemoglobin level is less than 5 %

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: In the first 24–48 hours after a major burn, fluid shifts from:
questions.rationale: Increased capillary permeability causes edema and hypovolemia.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Emergent Phase (PDF p. 407)
questions.quote: Fluid shift from intravascular to interstitial space causing hypovolemia

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which lab finding is expected in the emergent phase of burns?
questions.rationale: Cell damage releases K; hemoconcentration raises Hct; metabolic acidosis occurs.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Burn Diagnostics (PDF p. 408)
questions.quote: Hyperkalemia (K+ leaks into blood vessels)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Stress ulcer in a burn client is called:
questions.rationale: Diminished GI blood flow causes Curling's ulcer; Cushing's follows head injury.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, GI Changes in Burns (PDF p. 407)
questions.quote: Curling’s ulcer

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the leading cause of morbidity and death in thermal burns after resuscitation?
questions.rationale: Immunosuppression increases infection and sepsis risk.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Immunological Changes (PDF p. 407)
questions.quote: Sepsis continues to be the leading cause of morbidity

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the correct first aid for a fresh thermal burn?
questions.rationale: Cool with water; never ice, ointments, or salves.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Burn Emergency Procedure (PDF p. 408)
questions.quote: Never apply ice directly to the burn.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A worker splashes an alkali chemical on the arm. The first action is to:
questions.rationale: Remove clothing and irrigate with copious running water.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Chemical Burns (PDF p. 408)
questions.quote: Rinse all areas of the body that have come in contact with the chemical.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: In the RACE fire protocol, what does 'R' stand for?
questions.rationale: RACE: Rescue, Activate alarm, Confine, Extinguish.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Burn Emergency (PDF p. 408)
questions.quote: R- Rescue the patient
